leadIn: By the end of this lesson, learners will be able to:
objectives: Import the useMediaQuery hook from the @mui/material package into a React TypeScript component.
Define a media query string to target specific viewport breakpoints.
Invoke the useMediaQuery hook with a media query string to evaluate viewport conditions.
Store the boolean result from useMediaQuery in a component state variable.
Apply conditional rendering to display different UI elements based on the media query result.
Utilize TypeScript type annotations to ensure proper typing of the media query result.
Construct responsive UI components that adapt to different screen sizes.
Execute the useMediaQuery hook within a functional component to access viewport information.
Implement dynamic styling by applying CSS classes conditionally based on media query matches.
Control component behavior by using media query results in useEffect dependencies.
Return appropriate JSX structures that respond to changes in viewport dimensions.
Modify component layout and content organization in response to breakpoint changes.
